verdicts.recomputed: Own synthetic test on own K sequences (conf 1-5 uniform per trade; same maps 2/2.75/3.5/4.25/5% and 20/27/35/42/50x with feasibility walk-down), 76 days, mean P(<50%): NULL, 0 net: margin conf 63.8% (median x0.56) vs flat 30x 56.3% (x0.74) vs flat 35x 67.5% (x0.47); risk conf 2-5% 18.2% vs flat 3.5% 16.8% vs flat 2% 2.2%. NULL -cost: risk conf 80.0% vs flat 2% 63.6%; margin conf 90.4%. INFO (+0.05R/level): risk conf 9.9% vs flat 3.5% 16.9%; margin conf 54.5% vs flat 30x 56.4%. Mean L^2 actually used: conf 836, flat 30x 756, flat 35x 947.
verdicts.note: Numbers reproduce, but 'confidence -> leverage does worse than flat 30x when confidence is uninformative' is confounded: the 20-50x map has a higher average risk (mean L^2 836 vs 756). Against a flat leverage of the same nominal average (35x) the confidence map is better (63.8% vs 67.5%). Under the null, ruin is simply ordered by mean L^2 (margin rule) or mean r (risk rule); the confidence map adds only the small variance penalty (18.2 vs 16.8%). The real reasons not to map confidence to leverage are that it scales risk with L^2 under margin = L% and does nothing at fixed risk; the 'info' benefit is an assumed 0.05R/level, not a measurement. lens2/sizing/verify/v3_ruin.py confidence(), out/v3_conf.csv

verdicts.recomputed: Their s3_sequences.csv (15m+30m): K20 3.84, K30 4.28, K40 4.49, K50 4.60 trades/day on the same signal set. Under the risk rule a signal executable at 50x is always executable at 20x (liquidation farther away; margin r x E/(lpn x 20) < E for any r <= 5% and stop > 0.13%), so the extra trades cannot come from 'more signals becoming executable'. On the same 15m signals the ROE ladder exits sooner at higher leverage (held 10.98 bars at 50x vs 13.89 at 30x), which frees the single position slot for more signals. Rule numbers at r 1%: 0 net 0%, -cost 15.6% (5y cost) / 45.6% (today's cost).
verdicts.note: The recommended rule is sound in mechanics, but (a) the stated reason K20 vs K50 differs is wrong: it is the ROE ladder shortening holds at high leverage (+20% trades/day, so +20% cost drag per day), which is another reason for exits in R; (b) at today's cost the 1% ruin under 'edge = -cost' is ~46%, not 20%; (c) paperbot/policy.py already contains RecommendedPolicy (risk 1% per stop, 2R default TP, guards 3% daily loss / 5 losses -> 24 h cooldown) but it picks the LOWEST whole leverage whose margin fits, caps at 10x and uses a 3 ATR buffer, i.e. the opposite leverage choice; the owners must pick one and the AI-trader code should reuse that class rather than a third sizing path.

Notes give no per-strategy share of signals that can take >= 20x at 1h/4h, although that is what the owners' 4h rule needs (5y 4h at 20x: BTC 55%, ETH 25%, LTC 17%, BCH 11%, DOGE 8%, SOL 4%).

Notes repeat 'bootstrap (7-day blocks)' as the only uncertainty; the bigger uncertainty is the cost level (5y vs today) and the imposed edge, not the block length (mean block 1/10/28 days changes ruin by < 1 point).
missed: Live 4h executability excluded the 98 REJECTED_SIZING (and 30 unresolved) 4h signals; with all 207 live 4h signals only 58% fit 20x under the risk rule (53% margin rule), 17% fit 30x.
Today's cost per trade in R is ~1.5x the 5-year level (narrow stops); the -cost ruin at r 1% rises from ~16-20% to ~46%, r 2% to ~79%.

Under the house ROE ladder leverage changes holding time (50x exits ~20% sooner), hence trades/day and cost drag per day for a one-position trader; this, not executability, drives the K20/K50 difference.

paperbot/policy.py RecommendedPolicy already implements risk-per-stop sizing (1%, max 10x, lowest leverage that fits, 3 ATR buffer, R take-profit, daily-loss / losing-streak guards). The study's rule (highest 50/40/30/20x, 1 ATR buffer) contradicts it on leverage and buffer; neither was reconciled.
Crash-day 48 h trader losses are sums, not compounded equity (can exceed -100%).
Confidence -> leverage null comparison is confounded by a higher mean leverage; compare at equal mean risk.

Portfolio level: ruin is computed per trader. Duplicate / overlapping strategies (e.g. F11_RAID = F11_TSOUP = F13_RAID_PD, N-strategy overlaps) would make several AI traders hold the same position, so 1% each can be 3-5% on one event for the owners' total book; a cross-trader exposure cap per coin/direction is not discussed.

Mark-price liquidation and the liquidation clearance fee are not modelled; with stops 1 ATR inside liquidation at 50x a fast wick can fill the stop-market near the liquidation price (pessimistic crash fills reached -3 to -4R).
Small real-money accounts: qty steps (BTC 0.001 ~ $86-120) and minNotional will bind before brackets at r 1% on a few hundred dollars; the rule needs a 'skip if rounding changes risk by > x%' check.
Kill switch / daily loss cap was not simulated although the repo's RecommendedSettings already define 3% daily loss and 5-loss cooldown values.
